papers.title: The DYNAM-O Toolbox: Characterizing Individualized Neural Signatures in Sleep EEG.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Introduces DYNAM-O, an open-source toolbox for detecting transient oscillations in sleep EEG as time-frequency peaks, with feature histograms and dimensionality reduction for individualized signatures. In 112 adults, it replicated higher fast-spindle frequency in females and identified greater low-alpha transient oscillatory activity in females, a novel sex difference ignored by traditional analyses.

papers.title: Stress-recovery dynamics reveal a separatrix in transcriptomic landscapes across organs and aging
papers.summary: Young and aged mice were subjected to transient sleep deprivation, and transcriptomes from six organs were profiled immediately after stress and after recovery to map age- and organ-dependent temporal dynamics. Neural ordinary differential equation-inferred transcriptomic vector fields revealed distinct stability regimes, including a separatrix in young testis transcriptomes that bounds the region from which perturbed states can return toward control.

papers.title: Juvenile AAV-Mediated MEF2C Gene Replacement Ameliorates Selected Phenotypes in Mef2c-Haploinsufficient Mice
papers.summary: This study tested juvenile AAV-mediated delivery of MEF2C isoforms in Mef2c-haploinsufficient mice, finding improvements in social novelty, sleep, and selected brain measures, indicating modifiable phenotypes during the juvenile period.

papers.title: Assessing accelerometry as an alternative to electromyography for mouse sleep scoring
papers.summary: Assessed agreement between accelerometry and electromyography for manual mouse sleep scoring using hippocampal LFP; overall epoch-by-epoch accuracy exceeded 90% with kappa above 0.8. Accelerometry under-classified Wake by 4.92% and over-classified NREM sleep by 3.29%, indicating slight bias relative to EMG.

papers.title: Repeated morphine reorganizes sleep-wake states, cortical and central medial thalamic oscillations, and network synchronization in mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Examined how repeated morphine exposure reorganizes sleep-wake states, cortical and central medial thalamic oscillations, and network synchronization in mice across first and fourth injections and abstinence. Morphine promoted wake, suppressed NREM and eliminated REM sleep; cortex and thalamus dissociated in NREM, with corticocortical alpha synchronization decreased acutely and thalamocortical theta synchronization reduced after repeated exposure.

papers.title: Circadian control of dopaminergic signaling to the mushroom body regulates sleep through rhythmic Pka-C1 transcription in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Identified a circadian circuit mechanism in Drosophila whereby dorsal lateral clock neurons rhythmically inhibit PAM-γ5 dopaminergic neurons, which excite mushroom body γ-KCs via Dop1R to drive Pka-C1 transcription through Onecut. This creates a feedback cycle between transcriptional and neural activity rhythms that promotes daytime wakefulness.

papers.title: Partial sleep deprivation diminishes and uncouples neuronal activity and energy metabolism in the live mouse hippocampus
papers.summary: Using two-photon microscopy in live mice, the study longitudinally tracked spontaneous neuronal activity and tissue partial pressure of oxygen (pO2) in hippocampal CA1 during 7 days of partial sleep deprivation and 7 days of recovery. Partial sleep deprivation progressively reduced spontaneous neuronal activity while sustaining elevated tissue pO2, and after recovery neuronal activity did not return to baseline and oxygenation continued to increase, indicating uncoupling of metabolic and functional recovery.

papers.title: Sleep macro-architecture in sleep-deprivation-sensitive and sleep-deprivation-insensitive juvenile myoclonic epilepsy: A polysomnographic study.
papers.summary: Overnight polysomnography compared sleep macro-architecture in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) patients with versus without self-reported sleep-deprivation-triggered seizures and in healthy controls. Sleep-deprivation-sensitive JME patients showed lower N3 and reduced REM than controls, and sleep-deprivation-sensitive status independently predicted N3% after adjustment for sex and anti-seizure medication class.

papers.title: Xylazine Reshapes the Sleep and Respiratory Consequences of Chronic Fentanyl Exposure in a Sex-Dependent Manner.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Compared chronic fentanyl and xylazine alone and in combination in male and female mice, finding that co-exposure produced sex-dependent sleep architecture changes, exacerbated respiratory depression relative to fentanyl alone particularly in males, and increased peripheral FGF21. Yohimbine partially reversed sleep alterations in a sex-dependent manner.

papers.title: Suppression of corticospinal excitability by sleep spindles without increase in GABAergic inhibition.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using real-time EEG-triggered TMS during sleep, this study found that corticospinal excitability was suppressed during sleep spindles relative to spindle-free NREM sleep, with the lowest excitability during spindle falling phase and trough, but this was not accompanied by modulation of GABA-A receptor-mediated short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI). Slow oscillations increased excitability and reduced SICI irrespective of spindle presence.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian regulation of DNA repair and retrotransposons in neuronal genome stability and neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that sleep and circadian rhythms temporally regulate neuronal genome stability, focusing on clock-dependent DNA repair pathways, sleep-related chromosomal integrity, and sleep-wake-dependent retrotransposon activity such as LINE-1. It proposes that sleep provides a permissive state for genome-protective processes and discusses links to neurodegenerative disease, noting that much human evidence remains preclinical or correlative.

papers.title: SleepMambaNet: a lightweight multimodal framework for sleep staging and sleep disorder screening with multicenter validation.
papers.summary: The study developed SleepMambaNet, a lightweight multimodal framework combining efficient channel attention and bidirectional Mamba modules for automated sleep staging and exploratory sleep disorder screening from polysomnographic signals. It achieved high performance across public datasets and a multicenter clinical cohort, with accuracy up to 0.854 and Cohen's kappa up to 0.806, using only 0.47 million trainable parameters.

papers.title: [Microstructural characteristics of sleep electroencephalogram in obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhonghua er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This case-control study of 1,821 suspected OSA patients analyzed sleep EEG microstructural features and found that OSA patients exhibited increased PSD across multiple frequency bands and stages, with trends intensifying by severity, alongside higher slow wave oscillation density/duration/amplitude in N3 and lower sleep spindle density in N2, indicating cortical hyperarousal and thalamocortical dysregulation.

papers.title: Pre-sleep acute stress modulates sleep-dependent emotional memory.
papers.summary: This experimental study examined how acute pre-sleep stress affects overnight consolidation of emotional and neutral memories in 34 healthy adults. Pre-sleep stress was associated with longer slow-wave sleep, elevated high-frequency EEG power, reduced slow oscillation-spindle coupling, and altered associations between EEG power and memory retention, but did not change overall memory performance.

papers.title: Regional and network patterns of sleep-depth-associated brain diffusion changes: an EEG-informed multishell diffusion MRI study.
papers.summary: In 9 healthy adults who maintained sleep during simultaneous EEG and multishell diffusion MRI, deeper sleep (lower ORP) was associated with reduced white-matter fractional anisotropy and kurtosis fractional anisotropy, lower gray-matter diffusivities, and opposite kurtosis effects, with region-specific correlations forming a network primarily in frontocentral and medial frontal-cingulate areas.

papers.title: Sleep fragmentation frequency is associated with distinct immune, microbial, and barrier-related profiles in DSS-induced colitis in mice.
papers.summary: In DSS-induced colitis mice, low- and high-frequency sleep fragmentation were associated with distinct endpoint-specific profiles: both increased plasma corticosterone, while high frequency increased colonic Th2 proportions and low frequency increased MPO, without significant corrected differences in clinical colitis severity among DSS groups.

papers.title: Sleep spindle deficits in childhood absence epilepsy improve with antiseizure treatment and disease resolution.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of EEGs from 53 children with childhood absence epilepsy (CAE) and 87 controls, sleep spindle rates were reduced in active CAE across cortical regions, most prominently in frontal areas, and normalized after disease resolution. Spindle rate was inversely correlated with epileptic spike rate and varied with antiseizure medication exposure depending on disease state.

papers.title: A retrospective exploratory study of sleep spindles as an adjunctive diagnostic marker for narcolepsy type 1: a comparison with insufficient sleep syndrome.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared sleep spindle indices from overnight polysomnography in 14 patients with narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) and 9 with insufficient sleep syndrome (ISS) to differentiate them. Automated detection found significant between-group differences in C3 fast spindle duration during N2 and density during NREM sleep, with C3 fast spindle duration showing moderate discriminatory performance (AUC 0.754, sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 66.7%), suggesting automated spindle quantification may complement MSLT.

papers.title: Integrating Wearable Temperature, Activity, Melanopic Light, and Lifelog Data to Assess Circadian-Behavioral Coupling in Free-Living Conditions.
papers.summary: This study presents a multimodal wearable and lifelog monitoring workflow combining heat-flux temperature estimation, actigraphy, melanopic light measurement, and web-based lifelog entries to assess circadian-behavioral coupling in ten healthy young adults over one week. The wearable-derived temperature rhythm marker showed a mean absolute difference of 27.1 minutes compared to ingestible capsule gastrointestinal temperature, and exploratory analyses suggested light exposure, activity timing, and behavioral timing provide contextual information for interpreting coupling patterns.

papers.title: Proteoform plasticity modulates the temperature response in circadian timekeeping.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Biophysically characterized an isoform-specific intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of the Neurospora clock repressor FREQUENCY (FRQ) and compared interactomes of two FRQ isoforms, identifying a motif that when altered selectively disrupts timekeeping in a temperature-dependent manner. The findings support a model in which IDRs function as environmental rheostats to enhance clock robustness.

papers.title: The orexinergic system in Alzheimer's disease: from sleep disruption to accelerated neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: Reviews the role of the orexinergic system in Alzheimer's disease, linking sleep-wake dysregulation to amyloid-beta accumulation and neurodegeneration. Highlights preclinical and biomarker evidence, and discusses the potential of orexin-targeting interventions, though proof of disease-modifying effects remains limited.

papers.title: Differential maturation of mRGC pupillary constriction and circadian rhythmicity in typically developing human infants
papers.summary: Used non-invasive eye-tracking pupillometry and sleep diaries to measure mRGC-mediated pupillary responses to red and blue light in human infants aged 1–12 months. Found prolonged post-natal maturation of mRGC pathways for pupillary constriction that was separate from sleep/wake photoentrainment, with different developmental temporal dynamics.

papers.title: Multidimensional neuropsychological heterogeneity in obstructive sleep apnea: deep clinical phenotyping in a single-center cohort, population proteomic context, and depressive-burden risk stratification.
papers.summary: This study integrated clinical phenotyping, UK Biobank proteomics, machine learning, and PBMC transcriptomics in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Cognition was associated with apnea burden and TyG, while affective burden was more strongly associated with TyG; a depressive-burden risk model achieved cross-setting AUROC up to 0.809, though calibration was less stable, and 21 proteins were shared across cognition, depression, and anxiety outcomes.

papers.title: Jiao-tai-wan alleviates cognitive impairment induced by sleep deprivation through IL33-associated lipid metabolism and PTP1B/SYK/AKT signaling pathway.
papers.summary: Investigated the mechanism by which Jiao-tai-wan (JTW) alleviates sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment in mice. JTW improved behavior, upregulated IL33, enhanced microglial phagocytosis, reduced perineuronal net aggregation, and modulated lipid metabolism and the PTP1B/SYK/AKT signaling axis.

papers.title: [Daytime sleepiness with recurrent nocturnal fall-related injuries: a case report of somnambulism triggered by severe obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
papers.summary: This case report describes a 34-year-old man with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) who experienced somnambulism episodes and false-positive MSLT results. CPAP therapy eliminated somnambulism episodes, normalized sleep architecture, and corrected the MSLT result, suggesting that vPSG should be performed before MSLT in patients with sleepiness and abnormal nocturnal behaviors.

papers.title: Resting-EEG Characteristics and Classification Model Exploration for Tap Test Prediction in Communicating Hydrocephalus: A Small-Sample Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This pilot study used resting-state EEG to predict tap test responsiveness in 30 patients with communicating hydrocephalus. Responders showed higher alpha-band power correlated with CRS-R improvement, and linear models (logistic regression, SVM) achieved high AUCs (up to 0.982), matching or exceeding deep learning models, indicating that EEG spectral features are linearly separable and sufficient for prediction.

papers.title: Remodeling of the hepatic circadian transcriptome across the estrous cycle.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Explored the circadian transcriptome of mouse liver across the four phases of the estrous cycle, finding that the estrous cycle imposes a ~4-day rhythm on the 24-hour rhythmicity of a considerable proportion of the transcriptome, with largest differences between pre- and post-ovulation phases. Promoter analysis suggests core circadian transcription factors may drive both estrous-cycle and sex-dependent rhythmicity.

papers.title: Light at Night, Night Shift Work, and Cancer: Illustrating Cumulative Exposure to Circadian Disruption through a Thought Experiment.
papers.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
papers.summary: Presents a thought experiment, 'The city that never sleeps,' to illustrate why focusing solely on light at night or night shift work is reductionist, proposing chronodisruption (misalignment between external and internal time) as a link between both pathways and cancer. Outlines six practical steps for designing studies to evaluate cumulative chronodisruption doses, including potential biomarkers.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian rhythm characteristics in unaffected first-degree relatives of individuals with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared sleep quality, chronotype, and biological rhythms in 146 participants (44 relatives of schizophrenia patients, 47 relatives of bipolar disorder patients, and 55 controls). No significant group differences were found in overall sleep quality, chronotype, or biological rhythm measures, though relatives reported later habitual bedtimes and wake-up times, suggesting circadian characteristics are largely preserved in unaffected first-degree relatives.

papers.title: A context-aware temporal modeling through unified multi-scale temporal encoding and hierarchical sequence learning for single-channel EEG sleep staging.
papers.summary: Proposes TempoSleep, a context-aware framework for single-channel EEG sleep staging that combines multi-scale feature extraction with temporal modeling and uses class-weighted loss and data augmentation to address class imbalance. Achieves 89.72% overall accuracy and 85.46% macro F1-score, with a notable 61.7% F1-score for the N1 stage on SleepEDF datasets.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Modeling of Directed Transfer Entropy Connectivity for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children.
papers.summary: The Contextualized Transfer Entropy Network (CTE-Net) was developed to estimate directed EEG connectivity using a Transformer encoder and differentiable transfer entropy for ADHD classification in children. On a public pediatric EEG dataset, CTE-Net achieved 83.4% participant-level accuracy and 90.2% ROC-AUC, while reducing within-subject dispersion of connectivity representations by a median of 38.35% relative to raw EEG.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals cell-type-specific circadian rhythms and their disruption by acute misalignment in mouse aorta.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-sequencing of mouse aorta under aligned and acutely misaligned light-dark cycles identified hundreds of cycling genes in vascular smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and fibroblasts, with female SMCs showing higher rhythmicity and more cycling genes than males. Acute misalignment reduced cycling amplitudes and caused limited peak-time adaptation, alongside proteostatic stress signatures in SMCs and in vivo increases in vascular permeability and microvascular thrombus formation in males.

papers.title: Recommended sleep duration is associated with greater parasympathetic regulation in patients with hypertension.
papers.summary: In 74 hypertensive patients, those achieving recommended sleep duration (7-9 h) had significantly greater 24-hour high-frequency heart rate variability (parasympathetic activity) than short sleepers (<7 h), independent of age, sex, dyslipidemia, β-blocker use, and physical activity energy expenditure. The findings suggest adequate sleep supports autonomic regulation in hypertension.

papers.title: Association between minimum nocturnal heart rate and cerebral small vessel disease in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 630 patients with obstructive sleep apnea, 42% had cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). Older age and higher nocturnal minimum heart rate were independently associated with CSVD, with a model AUC of 0.752, indicating that elevated nocturnal minimum heart rate, possibly reflecting autonomic dysfunction, is linked to CSVD in OSA.

papers.title: Improved Sleep and Clinical Outcomes Following a Single-Session Intervention among Adolescents with Borderline Personality Disorder Features.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: A single-session sleep-focused intervention was tested in 57 adolescents with borderline personality disorder features and sleep difficulties, using ecological momentary assessment and at-home EEG. Post-treatment, multiple objective and subjective sleep indices improved, and several BPD symptom measures also improved significantly.

papers.title: The effects of coherent breathing and blue light after an acute stress on sleepiness and the stress response in a workplace setting: A randomized double-blind cross-over trial.
papers.summary: Evaluates a workplace stress management intervention combining 0.1 Hz coherent breathing and blue light exposure in a randomized double-blind crossover trial. The intervention significantly reduced subjective stress by 31.23%, decreased sleepiness by 0.84 points, and increased positive affect by 1.85 points, with no significant effects on negative affect or HRV.

papers.title: Lactobacillus reuteri ATG-F4 alleviates behavioral impairment induced by chronic stress.
papers.journal: The Korean journal of physiology & pharmacology : official journal of the Korean Physiological Society and the Korean Society of Pharmacology
papers.summary: Chronic stress in mice increased immobility frequency and reduced locomotor and exploratory behavior, while Lactobacillus reuteri ATG-F4 treatment maintained immobility at control levels, restored locomotion and exploration, reduced stress-enhanced sleep latency, and modulated brain expression of GABA and serotonin receptor genes and gut microbiota composition. The results indicate ATG-F4 ameliorates chronic stress-induced behavioral impairments, potentially via gut-brain mechanisms.

papers.title: Integrative genetic and inflammatory immunology profiling of type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with comorbid insomnia: A pathway-based analysis of infection susceptibility and clinical outcomes.
papers.summary: In a case-control study of 180 T2DM patients with comorbid insomnia, 180 T2DM patients without insomnia, and 120 healthy controls, integrated genetic and inflammatory profiling identified NF-kB, NLRP3 inflammasome, and TLR pathways as strongly co-activated in the comorbid group. T2DM-insomnia patients had a 3.8-fold higher 52-week cumulative infection incidence than healthy controls and 2.1-fold higher than T2DM-only patients, with IL-6, TNF-alpha, NF-kB activation, and regulatory T-cell depletion mediating 64% of the indirect effect.

papers.title: Exploratory EEG Feature Profiles During Viewing of Six Combined Indoor Spatial-Color Conditions.
papers.summary: An exploratory EEG workflow was developed to describe neural feature profiles during viewing of six combined indoor spatial-color conditions in 20 adults, using sequence-aware event mapping and multi-domain feature extraction. The study reports descriptive condition-level values and waveform summaries but no inferential results or pure color/room effects, emphasizing a traceable pipeline for future factorial validation.

papers.title: The trigger-timing framework for long COVID: using symptom triggers and temporal patterns to guide mechanistic stratification and treatment planning.
papers.summary: Proposes a conceptual trigger-timing framework for Long COVID that uses common daily stressors (e.g., upright posture, exertion, meals) and the timing of symptom worsening to infer dominant underlying mechanisms such as autonomic dysfunction, impaired recovery physiology, or mast cell-related processes. The framework is intended to guide mechanistic stratification, diagnostic evaluation, and treatment sequencing but remains hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
